content.short: Ceramic is a decentralized data network that brings unlimited data composability to Web3 applications.
content.description: Ceramic is a decentralized data network that enables unlimited data composability for Web3 applications. It supports apps that need to track data changes over time without relying on a centralized server, allowing data histories to be stored, referenced, and recomposed as needed. By composing static files into higher-order, mutable data structures, Ceramic lets developers program how data behaves and evolves, with the resulting state stored and replicated across a decentralized network of nodes to ensure availability, integrity, and resilience.

resources.title: How Pairwise Synchronization Improves Decentralized Data Management
resources.tldr: The team replaced the algorithm at the heart of the database, moving from multicast to pairwise sync. Explains what was wrong with the old approach and what the swap cost them.

resources.title: A Step-by-Step Guide to Ceramic's Private Data Proof-of-Concept
resources.tldr: Adding privacy to a network built around open, shared data is genuinely awkward. Walks through a deliberately minimal proof of concept rather than promising a finished feature.

resources.title: OrbisDB Is a Practical Upgrade for Databases on Ceramic
resources.tldr: What changes when you put a familiar database interface over a decentralised data network, and which of the usual guarantees survive that translation.
